Data.title: Analyst Blasts Strategy After CEO Signals New Priority Beyond Bitcoin
Data.body: It was precisely six years ago when a rather unknown company in the cryptocurrency industry at the time made a revolutionary change to its asset reserve strategy and adopted Bitcoin. The entity in question, called MicroStrategy back then, started to accumulate BTC en masse and only accelerated its purchases after the 2024 presidential elections in the US. The community became accustomed to hearing about new acquisitions made by the company, some of which were worth billions of dollars. Its total stash grew exponentially and currently sits at 843,775 units. Within this timeframe, BTC bulls consistently heard that the company (and its former CEO) would never sell… until they did . And then everything changed. During the most recent earnings call, the company hinted that it has plans to sell up to $5 billion in bitcoin, which is significantly higher than the previously claimed $1.25 billion. The Latest Shift Strategy (as it is called now) has gone five consecutive weeks without purchasing BTC, marking its longest acquisition pause in years. Instead of deploying capital into BTC, the firm has steadily increased its cash reserve through recent fundraising activities. As we previously reported , Strategy has been rebuilding its USD position while continuing to explore financial options tied to its expanding portfolio of preferred stock offerings. In the most recent official change, CEO Phong Le took to X to announce the company’s new primary corporate objective, which reads: “Our corporate objective is for STRC to trade at $99-$100 over time.” In the earnings call, he was more specific: “Our intent is to sell bitcoin for three reasons when we think it’s appropriate for the company. One, fund the U.S. dollar reserve up to $1.25 billion. Additional reasons include funding dividend and interest payments of $1.76 billion a year and funding up to $2 billion in common and preferred stock repurchases,” Le said, according to a FactSet transcript. The tweet and comments garnered immediate reactions from some well-known industry commentators as well as constant critic Peter Schiff, who was quick to determine that: “In other words, common shareholders are screwed.” Crypto Kaleo, though, a popular analyst who recently argued that Strategy would have to sell at least 50,000 BTC in the next couple of years to fund dividend payments, wasn’t so kind. In one tweet, he ironically asked whether the CEO remembers when the company’s primary corporate objective was to increase Bitcoin per share before adding : “It was only two months ago, so shouldn’t be difficult!” In another post, though, he brought the bashing to a higher level, claiming that Strategy is no longer a BTC company. Instead, it operates as a credit company, and its credit rating is “atrocious.” Strategy went from having a primary objective of increasing Bitcoin per share to trying to make sure their preferred shares trade back to $100… in just two months. They’re no longer a BTC company. They’re a credit company. And their credit rating is atrocious. https://t.co/fHoXr376QY — K A L E O (@CryptoKaleo) July 31, 2026 The comments below his post were split. Some agreed that Strategy is increasingly resembling a leveraged financial organization rather than a straightforward BTC holding company. Others defended the firm’s approach, noting that maintaining confidence in STRC is essential if Strategy wants to continue raising capital efficiently and safely for future crypto purchases. STRC Matters The Saylor-co-founded company launched STRC as part of its growing suite of preferred stock offerings designed to finance its long-term BTC accumulation strategy. However, it needs to trade at its par price of $100 to function properly, and it hasn’t been able to for months. It dumped below $75 at one point, before the company shifted its focus to rebuilding its USD reserve. It has since recovered to almost $90. As such, some investors view Le’s comments as a tactical, short-term objective rather than believing Strategy has abandoned its Bitcoin-focused vision. Still, the timing has fueled questions about the firm’s evolving identity and strategy, especially given the ongoing market uncertainty. Data.title: XRP Ledger 3.2.1 Goes Live to Tame Unknown Manifests as XRPL Closes In on 500K New Accounts in 2026’s First Half
Data.body: XRP Ledger Rolls Out Critical 3.2.1 Upgrade as Adoption Hits Record High The XRP Ledger has rolled out version 3.2.1, a critical security and stability update following an unusual validator manifest flood detected on July 31. Despite the incident, the network continued processing transactions and closing ledgers without interruption, underscoring the resilience of its infrastructure. According to XRP Ledger Operations, the issue arose because nodes accepted, stored, and re-broadcast an unlimited number of validator manifests linked to unknown validator keys. While the event posed no risk to consensus or transaction integrity, it unnecessarily consumed node memory, storage, and bandwidth. Why is Version 3.2.1 a game-changer? Well, it introduces four safeguards to prevent similar abuse. The update rejects oversized manifests, limits incoming manifest batches, caps the number of manifests shared during peer connections, and restricts the cache to 100 unknown validator keys. Unknown manifests are also no longer written to disk, preventing them from persisting after a node restart. As a result, node operators are encouraged to upgrade immediately, allow the server to run for one to two minutes, then perform a second restart to fully clear any previously stored unknown manifests. XRP Ledger 3.2.1 Arrives Amid Record Growth and Rising Institutional Demand The release comes as the XRP Ledger continues to expand despite a difficult market. In the first half of 2026, the network added 489,739 new accounts , growing from 7.91 million to 8.40 million before surpassing 8.42 million in July, a new all-time high. Notably, this growth occurred while XRP's price fell about 41%, signaling that network adoption continued independently of market performance. Other on-chain metrics point to strengthening fundamentals. XRP balances on exchanges have dropped to a seven-year low, tightening available supply, while spot XRP ETFs have attracted roughly $1.49 billion in cumulative inflows, reflecting sustained institutional demand. Ripple has also launched Ripple Mint , enabling enterprises to issue and manage RLUSD, its U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin. Institutional adoption is also broadening beyond payments. Insurance giant Aviva has chosen the XRP Ledger for a tokenized liquidity fund, reinforcing the network's growing role in real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. Furthermore, developers are bringing tokenized shares of companies including Tesla, NVIDIA, and SpaceX to the XRPL, while XRP and RLUSD are increasingly powering AI agent payments through emerging blockchain infrastructure. More than a routine maintenance release, XRP Ledger 3.2.1 highlights the network's ability to respond swiftly to operational challenges without disrupting service. Coupled with record account growth, rising institutional participation, expanding tokenization, and new enterprise financial products, the update further strengthens the XRP Ledger's position as a leading blockchain for tokenized assets and next-generation global payments.

Data.title: Football Crypto Betting Guide for the 2026–27 Season
Data.body: The 2026–27 football season arrives under circumstances that bettors rarely encounter. The expanded FIFA World Cup ended only a month before Europe's biggest leagues begin, forcing domestic competitions to adjust their calendars and clubs to rethink squad management. Premier League clubs, for example, have just over four weeks between the World Cup final and the opening fixture, leaving many international players with limited recovery time. For anyone betting with cryptocurrency, this creates opportunities alongside additional uncertainty. Fast deposits, instant settlements and live betting have become standard features of crypto sportsbooks, allowing bettors to react quickly as team news develops. Platforms such as Dexsport combine football markets with multi-chain payments, live betting, cash out functionality and transparent on-chain transactions in a single platform. This guide explains what makes the 2026–27 season different and what football bettors should pay attention to before placing their first wagers. A Season Unlike Any Other Most European leagues traditionally begin in early or mid August. This year, several competitions have delayed their opening weekends to accommodate players returning from the 2026 World Cup. The current schedule includes: La Liga opening on 14–16 August Premier League, Serie A and Ligue 1 beginning on 21–23 August Bundesliga starting on 28–30 August The compressed calendar means clubs have completed shorter pre-season tours, while many star players have barely had time to recover after representing their national teams. Why the World Cup Changes Everything International tournaments often influence club football during the following months, but the expanded 48-team World Cup amplifies that effect. Many elite footballers have played six or seven high-intensity matches before returning to their clubs. Coaches must balance fitness with performance, making squad rotation far more common during the opening weeks. A favorite may rest key attackers before an important Champions League fixture. Newly promoted clubs with fewer international players may actually enter August in better physical condition than title contenders. Odds often reflect club reputation more than current squad availability, particularly early in the season. Checking confirmed lineups thirty to sixty minutes before kickoff becomes more valuable than ever. Fixture Congestion Will Shape the Season Football's calendar continues to expand. Elite clubs now compete across domestic leagues, domestic cups, UEFA competitions and international breaks. Even without another major tournament, the number of matches remains exceptionally high. Rather than evaluating only league position, bettors should examine how many matches a team has played over the previous two or three weeks. Teams that continue winning may gradually create fewer chances, press less aggressively and rotate defenders. These subtle changes frequently become visible through performance statistics before bookmakers fully adjust their prices. Transfers Continue After Kickoff Another feature of modern football is that leagues begin before transfer windows close. A club may open the season with one striker and finish August with another. Defensive partnerships change, tactical systems evolve and new signings require time to adapt. Rather than assuming preseason form will continue throughout August, it is worth monitoring transfer activity until the window officially closes. Major departures sometimes create betting value before bookmakers fully incorporate their impact. Managerial Changes Create Uncertainty Several major clubs begin the season under new management. Every coach introduces different tactical ideas, pressing intensity and player roles. Some adapt immediately, while others require months before performances stabilize. Historical statistics remain useful, but they become less predictive when an entirely new system replaces the previous one. Early matches often provide better information than last season's numbers. Live Betting Continues to Expand Live betting has become one of the fastest-growing parts of football wagering. Markets now update within seconds after goals, substitutions, red cards and penalty decisions. Odds shift constantly throughout the match, rewarding bettors who closely follow the game instead of relying solely on pre-match analysis. Cash Out has also become a standard feature on many sportsbooks. Rather than waiting for the final whistle, bettors can secure part of their profit or reduce potential losses as a match develops. Used carefully, this provides greater flexibility than traditional fixed betting. Crypto Makes Football Betting More Flexible Cryptocurrency has changed how many bettors interact with sportsbooks. Instead of relying on traditional banking systems, users can fund accounts directly with Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT and many other digital assets. Deposits generally settle within minutes, withdrawals are often processed automatically and cross-border payments become much simpler. For bettors who regularly wager on international football, this reduces friction considerably, especially during busy weekends with matches across multiple leagues. The choice of supported cryptocurrencies has also expanded. Many sportsbooks now accept dozens of assets across several blockchain networks, allowing users to manage funds without unnecessary conversions. Why Dexsport Fits the 2026–27 Football Season Dexsport reflects many of the trends shaping modern crypto betting. The platform supports more than 100 betting markets on major football matches, alongside live betting, Cash Out functionality and live streaming for selected events. Players can deposit using more than 38 cryptocurrencies across 20 blockchain networks without completing mandatory KYC verification. Registration is available through email, Telegram or wallets such as MetaMask and Trust Wallet. Football sits alongside other popular sports including basketball, tennis, MMA and hockey, while esports markets cover titles such as CS2, Dota 2 and Valorant. The platform also maintains a public live betting desk where wagers and outcomes can be viewed transparently, adding an additional layer of visibility that distinguishes blockchain-based sportsbooks from many traditional operators. For bettors planning to follow an entire football season rather than a single tournament, features such as weekly cashback, Sports Club rewards and multi-chain support provide practical advantages over moving funds between different platforms throughout the year. Final Thoughts The 2026–27 season rewards preparation more than reputation. World Cup fatigue, shortened pre-seasons, transfer activity and fixture congestion make the opening months less predictable than usual. Bettors who follow lineup news, underlying performance metrics and scheduling pressures will have a clearer picture than those relying only on league tables or club names. Crypto sportsbooks complement this environment well. Fast payments, immediate access to live markets and flexible bankroll management allow bettors to respond quickly as information changes. Combined with careful analysis, those advantages can make a noticeable difference across a season that promises to be one of the most demanding football has seen in years. Data.title: Evernorth Makes Major Move for XRP Expansion
Data.body: Evernorth Holdings just put a price tag on its leadership team. Crypto pundit BankXRP (@BankXRP) flagged the news, posting about the company’s latest SEC filing. On July 29, Evernorth filed Amendment No. 5 to its Form S-4 registration statement with the SEC. The filing pushes its merger with Armada Acquisition Corp II closer to the finish line and reveals exactly how much its top executives stand to earn. The Nasdaq Push Evernorth wants to become the largest publicly traded XRP treasury company . The plan runs through a SPAC merger with Armada Acquisition Corp II. Once complete, the combined company will trade on Nasdaq under the ticker XRPN. Evernorth holds 473 million XRP tokens , built through purchases and contributions from Ripple. The company doesn’t just want to hold XRP and sit on it. It aims to grow its XRP per share through lending markets, liquidity provisioning, and validator operations on the XRP Ledger. Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin factors into that strategy too. JUST IN: Evernorth Holdings filed Amendment No. 5 to its S-4 with the SEC (July 29), advancing its SPAC merger with Armada Acquisition Corp II toward a Nasdaq listing under ticker XRPN. The filing discloses executive employment terms: Jessica Jonas (CLO) $400K base, 50% target… https://t.co/RtXdfxNR4o pic.twitter.com/9CJNJGPX2c — 𝗕𝗮𝗻𝗸XRP (@BankXRP) July 31, 2026 Who Runs Evernorth CEO Asheesh Birla spent over 25 years in Silicon Valley and helped scale Ripple from a startup to a company with over 1,000 employees. Chief Legal Officer Jessica Jonas built her career in commercial litigation before taking senior roles at Gemini and American Express. Chief Business Officer Sagar Shah spent nearly a decade in the XRP ecosystem at Ripple, where he helped launch RLUSD and led the acquisition of custody platform Metaco . Chief Operating Officer Meg Nakamura founded and ran Apto Payments, building card infrastructure for companies like Coinbase and Venmo. The Numbers Behind the Incentives The employment terms for Jonas, Shah, and Nakamura are intriguing. Jonas gets a $400,000 base salary, a 50% target bonus, and $4.5 million in RSUs. Shah and Nakamura each get a $300,000 base salary, a 50% target bonus, and $2.8 million in RSUs. Add those figures up and Evernorth just committed over $10 million in equity to three executives alone, on top of base pay and bonus targets. A 50% bonus target signals a company betting heavily on its executives hitting aggressive growth numbers before and after the Nasdaq listing. We are on X, follow us to connect with us :- @TimesTabloid1 — TimesTabloid (@TimesTabloid1) June 15, 2025 Is This Good for XRP? A Nasdaq-listed company built entirely around XRP gives institutional investors a regulated way to gain exposure to the token without holding it directly. Locking in executive pay tied to performance targets pushes Evernorth’s leadership to grow the company’s XRP holdings and generate yield through the XRP Ledger. A successful listing also sets a precedent. It shows XRP can support the same treasury company model that Bitcoin has used to attract institutional demand.
